It's still possible we get a great game, but the loss of Caleb Williams for this week due to a hamstring injury certainly takes away from the appeal of this one. It is worth noting this line has dipped a point even after the news that Williams would be out for several weeks. The Eagles should be able to score at least 24 points against the Bears and I just don't see how Chicago is going to find 20+ points with an offense led by a 38-year-old Case Keenum . Keenum is starting for the Bears this week , even though Tyson Bagent cleared concussion protocol and is available to play. I generally trust Ben Johnson to dial up enough trickeration to keep his team in a game where it doesn't have its star quarterback, but this feels like a terrible matchup. The Eagles are a boring boa constrictor, and that's a bad matchup for an undermanned team in prime time. Monday Night Football player props Case Keenum Over 0.5 interceptions (-122, DraftKings) I think the Bears would, in a perfect world, love to keep Keenum's pass attempts down and just run the heck out of the ball if they could, but neither the Commanders nor Titans were particularly effective on the ground against Philly. As such, I think Keenum's going to have to hoist the ball close to 30 times and that should provide an opportunity for the Eagles to jump a route or find a pick. This price is more than reasonable, especially if Keenum and the Bears are chasing points late. Dontayvion Wicks Over 41.5 receiving yards (-110, DraftKings) Wicks' Eagles career has started off in impressive fashion, with the former Packers receiver producing multiple games north of 70 receiving yards, slotting into the starting lineup for Philly and becoming a trustworthy weapon for Jalen Hurts alongside DeVonta Smith . I like him to clear this number against a Bears defense that has been extremely vulnerable to No. 2 receivers so far this season, at least when the weather's cooperated. The Eagles are not going to try and win this game by slinging the ball everywhere and cutting Hurts loose in the red zone. They're gonna want to pound the ball as much as they can and feed Barkley and maybe even Tank Bigsby (who is a decent price at +650). D'Andre Swift (-105, DraftKings) Nothing too fancy for us here, just some good, old-fashioned cheap touchdown scorers. Swift is priced at +100 and should be Keenum's best friend in this spot, given his ability to catch passes out of the backfield. I also considered Colston Loveland here, but I'm a little worried about the tight end rotation for the Bears. Plus, Swift can score rushing or receiving and should get plenty of action in both facets. Moton: Patriots (+3.5) It's understandable that the panel leaned heavily toward the Seahawks, given Seattle's dominant 29-13 victory over New England in Super Bowl LX seven months ago. Since then, the Seahawks have lost key parts of that team and coaching staff. Former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker, who led Seattle's backfield with 1,027 yards and five touchdowns, signed with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks also lost cornerback Riq Woolen and safety Coby Bryant in free agency. Meanwhile, the Patriots added wideouts A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Running back TreVeyon Henderson won't play because of an ankle injury, though Rhamondre Stevenson has handled a workhorse role in the past. New England covers the 3.5-point spread. Predictions Patriots: Moton Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams (in Australia) 2 of 16 AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford FanDuel Line: Rams (-3.5) Hanford: Rams (-3.5) There's no team entering the season with bigger hype than the Rams, and I'm buying it. While you could argue that their travel plans and a 49ers team that's probably more overlooked than it should be entering the season is a recipe for an upset, I think the Rams will show right away why they're the Super Bowl favorites. L.A. wins by a touchdown behind a dominant defensive performance. O'Donnell: 49ers (+3.5) Both teams have been major offseason headline generators: the Rams for building a super team headlined by the Myles Garrett trade and return of Aaron Donald; and the 49ers for what boils down to a lot of negativity headlined by injuries. In fact, while almost all the focus has been on George Kittle's potential return in Week 1, we don't actually know if Christian McCaffrey will be fit to play, and conventional wisdom would be to back the favorites. But these two teams traveled a long, long way to play a football game, and I'd rather take the points against a familiar foe in an unfamiliar setting regardless of who is on the field. Predictions 49ers: Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Rams: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans 3 of 16 AP Photo/David J. Phillip Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud FanDuel Line: Bills (-1.5) Davenport: Bills (-1.5) Laying points on the road against arguably the NFL's best defense is starting the season with some anxiety. But I have that much more anxiety about C.J. Stroud after how he finished last season—Josh Allen leads the Bills to a close win on one of Week 1's better games. Gagnon: Texans (+1.5) Week 1 is a lot of gut, and I have a feeling the Houston defense will be extremely prepared for Buffalo in the Texans' home opener. That was certainly the case when they beat the Bills at this very site in November 2025. The Bills are an excellent team, but this is a tough spot for their new coach. Predictions Bills: Davenport Texans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski TOP NEWS NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈 Bleacher Report 6h J.J.'s Vikings Tenure 'Brutal' Bleacher Report 5h Tyreek's Cryptic Tweet 🧐 Bleacher Report 1h Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers 4 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams FanDuel Line: Bears (-2.5) Moton: Bears (-2.5) The Bears enter this matchup with a shaky secondary. Safety Coby Bryant underwent knee surgery and will miss a few months of action. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon is on the physically unable to perform list with a calf injury. However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young hasn't shown the ability to exploit opposing pass defenses' weaknesses, averaging just 180.2 passing yards per game over his three-year career. Bears go on the road with their ascending offense and win by at least a field goal. Sobleski: Bears (-2.5) The Carolina Panthers finished among the bottom six in total offense last season. The organization added next-to-nothing to improve the unit. If anything, the group might be worse since both offensive tackle spots remain a serious concern. Conversely, the Chicago Bears are explosive enough offensively to easily cover this spread. Predictions Bears: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars 5 of 16 AP Photo/Gary McCullough Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence FanDuel Line: Jaguars (-7.5) Gagnon: Jaguars (-7.5) I think the Browns could have some surprisingly nice moments this season, but this ain't the spot. Cleveland is, at the very least, a work in progress as a new core and coaching staff settle in. The Jaguars, on the other hand, are a well-oiled machine on a strong trajectory following a superb second half to the 2025 campaign. I expect them to keep rolling in their home opener. Sobleski: Browns (+7.5) Despite every expectation of the Cleveland Browns' offense imploding thanks to questionable quarterback setup, Todd Monken's squad gets the benefit of the doubt in the head coach's debut because of its defense. Myles Garrett might be gone, but this unit still has playmakers at all three levels to slow the Jaguars and make the contest interesting. Predictions Browns: Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers 6 of 16 AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers FanDuel Line: Steelers (-3.5) Gagnon: Falcons (+3.5) I don't trust the Steelers, and I hate that hook for them. It's really that simple. These teams are closer to being evenly matched than many might believe, and the Steelers were far from impressive at home in 2025. The Falcons didn't lose by more than a field goal in regulation in any of their last six road games last season. They should keep this game tight. Hanford: Steelers (-3.5) The jury is out on Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy's reunion in Pittsburgh and the impact it will have on a stagnant Steelers offense, but I just don't see the "winner" of the NFL's least inspiring QB battle, Tua Tagovailoa, doing serious damage to the Steelers defense. I expect this game to be ugly, like most Steelers games, but Tagovailoa makes one too many mistakes as Pittsburgh improves to 6-1 ATS in its last seven games against Atlanta. Predictions Falcons: Gagnon Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New York Jets at Tennessee Titans 7 of 16 AP Photo/George Walker IV Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward FanDuel Line: Titans (-1.5) Davenport: Jets (+1.5) Fans who watch this entire game should receive some sort of reparations from the NFL. Neither offense in this slopfest can be trusted even a little, but for my money the Jets are slightly better defensively. First team to 13 points wins! Knox: Titans (-1.5) I'm inclined to believe it when I see it with Robert Saleh, Cam Ward, and the Titans. However, I believe they at least have the potential to turn things around quickly. The Jets? Not so much. I believe that New York is playing for 2027 and beyond. I don't envision Tennessee running away with this one, but I don't see the Jets winning on the road, and this is awfully close to a pick'em. Predictions Jets: Davenport Titans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions 8 of 16 AP Photo/Caroline Brehman New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough FanDuel Line: Lions (-7) Hanford: Saints (+7) The Saints closed last season red hot, and while some of that may be fool's gold, I think they'll keep this one within a touchdown. I expect Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Co. to have success against the Saints' defense, but I don't trust the Lions' secondary to give Tyler Shough major issues. Lions win by six in a high-scoring game. O'Donnell: Lions (-7) Hey, the Saints are going to be feisty, and the panel is just about split on the Lions giving this many points for good reason. Missing the playoffs a year ago should be gnawing at Dan Campbell's group, though. Detroit scored an average of 32-plus points per game at home last season — a full touchdown more than on the road. Can the Saints go toe-to-toe in a shootout with the Lions in Detroit? Maybe, but I'll back a first-week barrage from the stronger offensive unit as the Lions look to set the tone for a rebound campaign. Predictions Saints: Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, O'Donnell Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals 9 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow FanDuel Line: Bengals (-3.5) Knox: Buccaneers (+3.5) If Joe Burrow can stay healthy, Cincinnati's new-look defense should make the Bengals legitimate AFC contenders. However, the Bengals have been notorious for slow starts under Zac Taylor. I can't envision them winning big against a Buccaneers team that can play the underdog card after missing the playoffs in 2025. Sobleski: Bengals (-3.5) Joe Burrow and Co. should hit the ground running. Can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers do the same without Mike Evans on the roster? Obviously, quarterback Baker Mayfield has other weapons in Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan. However, the Cincinnati Bengals still have an advantage in offensive firepower with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who were both back at practice this week. Predictions Buccaneers: Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell Bengals: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, Sobleski Baltimore Ravens at Indianapolis Colts 10 of 16 AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson FanDuel Line: Ravens (-3.5) Hanford: Ravens (-3.5) Backing this many favorites at 3.5 makes me antsy, but I think the Ravens will be too much for the Colts here. I'm not sold on the Ravens overall this season, but I think their improved defense under Jesse Minter, with the addition of Trey Hendrickson, should give them enough punch to make life very difficult for Daniel Jones. Lamar Jackson has to get back on track as a passer this season, but I think he makes enough plays to put Baltimore over the top. Sobleski: Colts (+3.5) Interestingly, the Indianapolis Colts' defense has a very specific matchup in its favor, with the defensive tackle duo of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart facing two brand-new starters along the Baltimore Ravens' offensive line. Thus, the Colts could control the line of scrimmage to make life difficult on quarterback Lamar Jackson and running back Derrick Henry. Offensively, Indianapolis should have all of its pieces back in place to get off to a hot start, as it did last season. Predictions Ravens: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton Colts: Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles 11 of 16 AP Photo/Daniel Kucin Jr. Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels FanDuel Line: Eagles (-5.5) Hanford: Eagles (-5.5) The Eagles have a lot of questions to answer on the offensive side of the ball in Week 1, but I'm just not buying the Commanders yet. Jayden Daniels is healthy, which will help, but the weapons around him leave some to be desired, and the absence of star LT Laremy Tunsil will loom large against an Eagles defense that loves to get after the quarterback. I'm not sure Jalen Hurts silences the critics in Week 1, but I do think the Eagles have enough juice in the run game and on defense to control the game and win by a touchdown. Moton: Commanders (+5.5) This is a divisional matchup, and both quarterbacks are learning new offenses. Expect both teams to be inefficient in a game of missed opportunities, while both defenses capitalize on miscues with takeaways. Philadelphia also lost some offensive explosiveness when it traded three-time Pro Bowl receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. On the ground, running back Saquon Barkley helps the Eagles grind out a close victory by a margin short of a touchdown. Predictions Commanders: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Eagles: Davenport, Hanford Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings 12 of 16 AP Photo/Abbie Parr Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson FanDuel Line: Vikings (-1.5) Davenport: Packers (+1.5) Neither of these teams are especially easy to trust in the early-going this year—the Vikings have a new quarterback in Kyler Murray and the Packers have significant questions on defense, especially where the pass rush is concerned. I'll take the points—with exactly zero confidence. Gagnon: Vikings (-1.5) I don't know how I feel about the Packers opening the season on the road against a sneaky-good division rival without Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons. Throw in the unpredictability factor with Kyler Murray, and I think Green Bay is in a tough situation here. Predictions Packers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell Vikings: Davenport, Sobleski Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders 13 of 16 AP Photo/John Locher Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty FanDuel Line: Raiders (-3.5) Moton: Raiders (-3.5) According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers is expected to miss "a game or two" after undergoing a trim on his meniscus. On a positive note from the injury front, head coach Klint Kubiak is optimistic about running back Ashton Jeanty suiting up after he suffered an ankle injury during practice on August 23. Without Bowers, expect the Raiders to feature Jeanty (if healthy) and rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. on the ground, which should be enough to control time of possession. The Miami Dolphins offense may not see much time on the field. Although the Raiders have an unproven secondary, with rookie second-rounder Treydan Stukes likely to play at safety and second-year pro Darien Porter at the No. 2 cornerback spot, quarterback Kirk Cousins is more equipped to dice up a shaky pass defense than Malik Willis. O'Donnell: Dolphins (+3.5) Woof. Two organizations in complete rebuild mode. Two new starting quarterbacks under new coaching staffs. Just give me the points in this one, and I'll figure out what to do with these two for the rest of the season after Week 1. Predictions Dolphins: Hanford, O'Donnell Raiders: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers 14 of 16 AP Photo/Gregory Bull Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert FanDuel Line: Chargers (-9.5) Davenport: Cardinals (+9.5) To be clear, the Arizona Cardinals have about as much chance of winning this game as I do of winning an Academy Award. But Arizona has talent on offense and showed it can move the ball last season—Jacoby Brissett will lead a garbage-time touchdown drive late and the Redbirds will sneak in the back door for the cover. Moton: Chargers (-9.5) Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been teammates with his top pass-catchers for multiple years, and the team added tight end David Njoku, who has 384 receptions for 4,062 yards and 34 touchdowns in his nine-year career. With newly established offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel calling the plays, the Chargers could score in flurries against the Cardinals, who retained defensive coordinator Nick Rallis after his unit gave up the fourth-most points last season. Predictions Cardinals: Davenport, Hanford Chargers: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants 15 of 16 AP Photo/Rick Scuteri Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott FanDuel Line: Cowboys (-2.5) Knox: Cowboys (-2.5) Will the Giants be better under new head coach John Harbaugh? Yes. Are they prepared to keep pace with a team that has one of the NFL's top offenses and a vastly improved defense? At this point in the season, I don't believe so. Week 1 divisional matchups can be unpredictable, and I won't be shocked if the Giants steal this one. I think it's far more likely that Dallas makes one or two defensive plays that it wouldn't have made a year ago to preserve a one-score victory. O'Donnell: Giants (+2.5) The Cowboys are the better team on paper, and the Giants' secondary will have a hard time defending CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens even if Big Blue is getting to Dak Prescott. But if a new coaching staff and the return of two injured star players to the lineup (Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers), on top of two rookie first-round picks starting in their debuts (Arvell Reese and Francis Mauigoa), at home on Sunday Night Football against a bitter rival, isn't enough to get a team up, then what in the gorydamn hell are we playing this game for? Predictions Cowboys: Davenport, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Giants: Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs 16 of 16 AP Photo/Jack Dempsey Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix FanDuel Line: Chiefs (-2.5) Knox: Broncos (+2.5) Winning as the road team in Kansas City is tough, but defense travels, and the Broncos have one of the best in the business. Beyond that, I think it's going to take a few games for Patrick Mahomes to find his groove with whatever post-injury playing style he brings to the 2026 season. The Chiefs will go as Mahomes does, and one or two instances of him hesitating behind the line will sink them against arguably the most well-rounded team in the conference. O'Donnell: Chiefs (-2.5) The Denver defense is going to be a problem for Kansas City, especially with a less than 100% healthy Patrick Mahomes back under center. On paper, the Broncos might be the better all-around team, too. And the Chiefs have lost two of the last three season openers, with the lone victory being a controversial end-of-game call that gave K.C. the victory over Baltimore in 2024. Yeah, all things point to a Broncos cover, if not an outright win. So, I'll ride with the minority and lay these points with the home team covering late. Despite the sample size growing, sportsbooks are still not paying attention to the new usage of certain players, leading to bad lines on Week 3 player props I am off to a 5-1 start on my player prop picks using this method – players who are outperforming their historical averages See the two best NFL player props to bet for Week 3 below As we enter Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, sportsbooks are starting to build a bit of a better sample size of each player’s new role/opportunity/ceiling/floor for the current season. While many players are producing at a very similar rate to what they have in the past, there are some players who have seen their production dramatically improve. When those players are not household names, who are posting massive stat lines, they don’t always catch the attention of sportsbooks, since they have a lot of betting lines to set every day. I have gotten off to a hot start this season (5-1) by simply identifying the players who sportsbooks have not adjusted to yet, and are still relying on past seasons to guide their prop markets. I have found another two players for Week 3 whose player prop markets do not match their expanded role and opportunity through the first two weeks. NFL Player Prop Picks for Week 3 Player Team Matchup Prop Market Over/Under Line Pick Josh Allen BUF LAC @ BUF Passing Yards 239.5 Over Adonai Mitchell NYJ NYJ @ DET Receiving Yards 45.5 Over Both Josh Allen and Adonai Mitchell have outperformed their Week 3 prop markets by a notable margin over the first two weeks of the 2026 NFL season. However, sportsbooks are still setting low over/unders for them this week. I am taking advantage of the opportunity by taking the over on both of these player props, and I believe these are the two best player props to bet for this slate of games. You can keep reading below for the full data breakdown and analysis to see how much better these two players have performed versus these lines. Josh Allen, QB, Buffalo Bills – Over 239.5 Passing Yards 2025 Passing Yards Per Game Avg: 215.8 2025 L5 Games Passing Yards Per Game Avg: 167.2 2026 Passing Yards Per Game Avg: 291 2026 Avg vs Betting Line: +51.5 (+21.5%) Josh Allen is thriving in 2026, as are his odds to win NFL MVP , thanks to Joe Brady taking over as head coach, and employing a much more aggressive offensive approach than what he was allowed to as OC under Sean McDermott. So far, Allen is averaging 291 passing yards per game, which is 51.5 yards more than his Week 3 passing yards market, and it’s a result of the extra 2.9 pass attempts per game he is averaging versus last year, along with Brady’s system calling for him to push the ball downfield more. This is evident from his intended air yards per attempt going from 7.28 last season to 10.22 through the first two games. The Bills’ QB has gone over 239.5 passing yards in each of his first two games this year, throwing for 334 in Week 1 and 248 in Week 2. Neither of the two defenses he played – the Texans and Lions – appear to be a whole lot worse than the Chargers defense, who he is preparing for this week. LA has allowed 265 gross passing yards per game this season. Here’s what that looked like per game: Week Opponent Gross Passing Yards Allowed by LAC 1 Arizona Cardinals 277 2 Las Vegas Raiders 253 For further context, Jacoby Brissett threw for 95 yards in Week 2 against the Seahawks, and Kirk Cousins totaled 160 passing yards in Week 1 against the Dolphins. So, it’s not like LA has just been forced to deal with prolific passing attacks through the first two weeks. The Chargers’ opponents have also both played with positive game scripts as well. Even if Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense do not keep up with Buffalo’s offense, this line is still too low for Allen. I’m also not concerned about the Bills likely being without DJ Moore for this one. There are still plenty of receivers who will get open in Brady’s system. Adonai Mitchell, WR, New York Jets – Over 45.5 Receiving Yards 2025 Receiving Yards Per Game Avg: 28.3 2025 L5 Games Passing Yards Per Game Avg: 29.4 2026 Passing Yards Per Game Avg: 61.5 2026 Avg vs Betting Line: +16 (+35.2%) When Adonai Mitchell was traded to the Jets last season, he landed with a team who trusted him. Shane Steichen, head coach of the Colts, did not trust Mitchell and was not even giving him many snaps each game. While Mitchell’s opportunity improved immediately in New York, simply by being on the field, his quarterback situation was rough. But that has changed this season too, as Geno Smith is a serviceable quarterback. The end result has been an extra 2.9 targets per game versus his average from last season, and he’s benefitting to the tune of 61.5 receiving yards per game through his first two, which is +16 yards versus his over/under for Week 3. Mitchell has been pretty consistent too, as he posted 60 yards in Week 1 and then 63 yards in Week 2. His matchup against the Lions at Ford Field on Sunday heavily favors aerial production, and playing in a dome removes any weather variables. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Expert Picks 2026 Texans vs Bills Prediction: Houston Texans Moneyline (-105) Based on the Texans’ defensive advantages over a normally strong Bills offense and Buffalo’s lackluster defensive record, my Texans vs Bills prediction is the Texans Moneyline (-105) . When these teams met in Week 12 last year, Buffalo’s offense struggled immensely. For the entire 2025 regular season, Buffalo recorded the following advanced metrics: +0.145 EPA per play and 48.2% success rate, including 50.5% dropback success rate. When the offense went up against Houston: -0.164 EPA per play, 36.9% offensive success rate, 35.6% dropback success rate. Dalton Kincaid missed the game for Buffalo, which in theory should provide a boost. However, Houston also operated without safety Jalen Pitre as a six-point underdog. Davis Mills and Woody Marks combined to move the ball effectively on Buffalo’s defense. The ground game in particular proved very efficient, producing a 54.2% rushing success rate. Comparatively, Houston produced a 35.6% rushing success over the entire season. David Montgomery’s arrival, plus some new pieces along the offensive line, should allow for continued offensive success by the Texans. A change from Mills to C.J. Stroud adds to the ceiling case. Meanwhile, the Texans defense directly mitigates all the strengths of Buffalo’s offense. Buffalo’s normally reliable offensive line faces one of the best pass rushes in the NFL. Reed Blankenship arrives to play safety after a strong tenure with the Eagles, while Jadeveon Clowney adds depth at edge. Those additions lead me to expect another strong performance from the Texans defense. It leads me to predict a third straight Houston win against Buffalo. Presuming Kyler Murray starts, it should open up the passing game against weak Green Bay corners. Late last year, bettors saw the secondary struggle without a coherent pass rush. From Week 13 onward – a sample that includes Parsons – the Packers ranked 28th in EPA per play and 29th in defensive success rate. That includes a Week 15 trip to Denver where Bo Nix shredded Green Bay for over 300 yards and four touchdowns. What really worries me about the Packers is the offensive line. The unit lost Rasheed Walker and Elgton Jenkins a season after ranking 25th in PFF’s pass-blocking grades. Romeo Doubs, Dontayvion Wicks and Emmanuel Wilson all departed as well. It leaves Jayden Reed, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson to try and exploit a strong defense. If you go back two seasons, Green Bay never produced much offensively until the game was out of reach. The Packers lost 31-29 in Week 4, but won the fourth quarter 22-3. Then they fell 27-25 in Minnesota, but won the fourth quarter 15-0. Those performances also came with superior skill players and a better offensive line compared to this matchup. Ultimately, Green Bay possesses the worst unit on the field in a Parsons-less defense. If you’re Cincinnati, the concern here is that Joe Burrow faced minimal snaps against blitz-heavy teams last year. Bowles blitzed at a 30.7% rate in 2025, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. When the Bucs didn’t blitz, the defense generated pressure at the league’s 17th-highest rate. Tampa Bay used draft picks and free agency to try and bolster the pass rush. It’ll have to work to force quick throws as it’s my belief Cincy’s receivers pose a mismatch for Tampa’s corners. However, Vea poses a massive challenge for a weak Bengals interior. Both he and first-round pick Ruben Bain Jr. could pose problems for the entire offensive line. If the Bucs force Burrow into short throws, it likely leads to fewer chunk plays that correlate with a high-scoring game. Where I’m more confident is the Bengals defense doing enough to keep Tampa’s offense at bay. While the Bucs’ offensive line remains amongst the best in the league, clear weaknesses exist. Those shortcomings sit along the interior, which will face Dexter Lawrence. How they’ll cope with that matchup remains to be seen, but it’s a nightmare on paper. That’s even before we get to the fact Tampa Bay lost Mike Evans in free agency. Additionally, Cincinnati posted decent defensive metrics toward the end of last season. Early in the year, the Bengals played terribly. But against good opponents in Weeks 12-17, they played serviceably. Over that timespan, the Bengals ranked 25th in EPA per play and 16th in success rate. Those games include three of nine opponent touchdowns via defense or special teams. Broaden the sample to include games against Pittsburgh and Cleveland at each end and the figure rises to seven of nine touchdowns. Laremy Tunsil is likely done for the season. Outside Jayden Daniels, Washington is relying on an aging skill group to take on one of 2025’s top defensive units. Philadelphia finished seventh in defensive DVOA last season, their second under DC Vic Fangio. En route to a Super Bowl win in 2024, the Eagles led the NFL. Late last year, the Eagles kept much better offenses under this number. Green Bay scored seven points. The Lions and Bills both stayed under 12.5 points. Albeit on short rest, Washington scored 18 on TNF two years ago at Lincoln Financial Field. More worrisome is how Washington gets the ball back from Philadelphia to score points. The defense has consistently ranked amongst the league’s worst. Minimal changes occurred this offseason to expect an uptick in quality. If coverage holds up downfield, there should be at least one opportunity for him to tuck the ball and take the free yardage available in front of him. It's essentially a bet that one play breaks correctly over four quarters. Pick: Sam Darnold Longest Rush Over 5.5 Yards (-107) Jadarian Price Over 53 Rushing Yards (-110) Seattle spent the final pick of the first round on Jadarian Price for a reason. The rookie averaged 6.0 yards per carry during his final season at Notre Dame, and his opportunity has grown entering Week 1. With Seattle leaning on Price as a major part of its backfield, there should be enough volume available for him to threaten this number. Even if New England is leading, Seattle doesn't need to abandon the run immediately. Price should receive enough early-down opportunities to threaten 54 yards, and his explosiveness gives him the ability to knock out a large portion of this number on one carry. Pick: Jadarian Price Over 53 Rushing Yards (-110) NFL Parlay Pick: Both Quarterbacks Throw an Interception (+265) The first parlay attacks both quarterbacks, despite them both being MVP -caliber players. Drake Maye to throw an interception Sam Darnold to throw an interception Odds: +265 This lines up nicely with my broader Patriots vs. Seahawks prediction, as I expect an aggressive, high-scoring game between two projected playoff teams. More passing attempts create more opportunities for mistakes. Seattle intercepted Maye twice in the Super Bowl and consistently pressured him. New England will undoubtedly have a better plan Wednesday, but that doesn't mean Maye plays mistake-free football. On the other side, if the Patriots jump ahead as I'm predicting, Darnold could eventually be put into obvious passing situations. That's exactly when defenses have opportunities to create turnovers. We don't need either quarterback to have a bad game. One mistake each turns this into a +265 winner. Pick: Maye & Darnold Each to Throw an INT (+265) NFL Touchdown Parlay for WNF: Stevenson & Price (+333) The second parlay goes straight to the running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson Anytime TD Jadarian Price Anytime TD Parlay Odds: +333 Stevenson is particularly appealing, with TreVeyon Henderson ruled out because of an ankle injury. Stevenson scored nine total touchdowns last season and should be one of New England's primary options near the goal line. Price has a chance to immediately take on a significant rushing role for Seattle. Rather than trying to predict which receiver Darnold targets near the goal line, I'm taking the rookie back to convert one of his opportunities. Both offenses scoring at least a few touchdowns fit perfectly with an Over 44.5 game script. At +333, we're getting better than 3-to-1 odds simply by asking both lead backs to find the end zone once. Pick: Stevenson & Price Anytime TD Parlay (+333) Best Wednesday Night NFL Bets The theme across the card is offense. The straight props offer several ways to attack that script individually, while the two parlays provide considerably more upside for bettors looking for plus-money action to open the NFL season. Eight of his 11 playoff berths have coincided with division titles, too, including last year’s. Denver is sitting at +225 to repeat as AFC West champions, which is good for third behind both the Chiefs and Chargers. However, the Broncos actually account for 34% of the bets to win the AFC West, narrowly outpacing the Chiefs and Chargers’ respective 32%. And in terms of the total handle, Denver leads the pack at 40%, signifying a sharp lean in their favor. Analysis We are entering Year 3 of Sean Payton and Bo Nix, not to mention all the other returning skill position players. Denver also went out and added Jaylen Waddle to supplement Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr., Lil’Jordan Humphrey, Evan Engram, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. They also bring back most key contributors from their defense, even using their top draft pick on Tyler Onyedim to make up for lineman John Franklin-Myers leaving in free agency. Considering that unit held opponents to the third-fewest points per game last season, it’s easy to see them being elite again in 2026. Going against a Chargers squad that hasn’t won a division crown since 2009 and a Chiefs team that showed signs of age and injury in 2025, the Broncos should be in the driver’s seat once again in 2026. Best AFC West Playoff Future Chargers to Make the Playoffs (-168) Betting Splits Ranking Bets 11th Handle 18th Why bettors are backing the Chargers The Chargers rank around the middle of the pack in terms of both bets and handle when it comes to making the playoffs. They are slightly above average with the 11th-most Make the Playoff bets and rank slightly below average with the 18th-most handle in that market. What is worth noting, however, is that they account for the third-fewest bets to miss the playoffs, as well as the smallest handle in that market. Basically, very few people and even fewer sharp bettors are banking on Los Angeles to miss the playoffs. Analysis Los Angeles went 11-6 in each of Jim Harbaugh’s first two seasons at the helm, earning a Wild Card berth both times. Dating back to Harbaugh’s time in charge of the 49ers, he has led his team to the playoffs in five of six opportunities. The Chargers also enter this campaign in a much healthier position than they were in last year, in which they thrived despite their offensive line issues. Pro Football Focus ranked their O-line 30th out of 32 units in the NFL, with Joe Alt missing 11 games and Rashawn Slater missing all 17. Their respective returns – plus the arrival of offensive guru Mike McDaniel at coordinator – could vault Justin Herbert into the league’s top tier of quarterbacks. Omarion Hampton might break out as well, if first round pick Jake Slaughter can replace the retired Bradley Bozeman and injured Tyler Biadasz at center. The Chargers have boasted a top-10 scoring defense in both of Harbaugh’s seasons, too, so there’s reason to believe they can weather the losses of Da’Shawn Hand and Otito Ogbonnia up front. Best AFC West Win Total Bet Raiders Over 5.5 Wins (-146) Betting Splits Percentage Bets 73% Handle 91% Why bettors are taking the over The majority of bettors are putting their money on the Raiders to win at least six games, despite the fact that they won just four games in 2024 and three in 2025. But with Antonio Pierce and Pete Carroll gone and reigning Super Bowl champion offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak now in charge, things could be different in Vegas. On top of the general public support, there is a pretty substantial sharp lean in the Raiders’ favor. 91% of the handle is on the Raiders to clear 5.5 wins, which is about as close to universal support as you can get from a total money perspective. Analysis Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza may be at polar opposite ends of their careers, but their arrivals are reason for confidence in Las Vegas. The top rookie and seasoned veteran should fit nice into Kubiak’s system, which brought Sam Darnold back from the dead in Seattle. Although they may not have the weapons to cobble together an elite offense, the Raiders have Kolton Miller returning at left tackle and Tyler Linderbaum entering the fray at center. That should give them an O-line that PFF ranks higher than No. 32, like they did last season, beyond Kubiak’s offense traditionally minimizing talent deficiencies up front. The Raiders have the Browns, Cardinals and Titans on the schedule after Thanksgiving, at which point the team will probably have come into its own. Games against the Jets, Saints and Dolphins look winnable as well, to say nothing of any potential upsets. Keep an eye on Week 18 against the Chiefs, when Kansas City may have already locked up their playoff seeding. Best AFC West Player Prop Bet Fernando Mendoza Under 12.5 Passing TDs (-110) Betting Splits Percentage Bets 4% Handle 43% Why bettors are backing the under There isn’t widespread support in Fernando Mendoza coming in under 12.5 passing touchdowns, with only 4% of the bets in that market coming in on that side of the line. There is a massive sharp lean, however, with 43% of the handle on the under. So while the public as a whole is getting swept up in the hype for the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, the people putting more money behind their bets aren’t quite as convinced. Analysis While there is reason to believe the Raiders will take a leap forward in 2026, their new franchise quarterback might not have a lot to do with it. Cousins, who is freshly 38 years old, started 14 games in 2024 and appeared in 10 in 2025. He led Atlanta to a 12-10 record when he started, despite all of that coming after his 2023 Achilles surgery. Cousins posted an unimpressive 87.2 passer rating during his time with the Falcons, a noticeable decline from his 99.9 mark between 2015 and 2023, but he was still a steady enough veteran presence to start over Michael Penix Jr. when healthy. Based on the start of training camp and the preseason, the starting job in Las Vegas belongs to Cousins. The Raiders also have a pretty tough schedule through their Week 13 bye, which would make installing Mendoza particularly difficult. I think the rookie sees the field in 2026, but not in any serious capacity until the final five games. So unless Cousins gets hurt, Mendoza probably won’t have much of a chance to stuff the stat sheet this season. Best AFC West Award Bet Patrick Mahomes to Win Comeback Player of the Year (+185) Betting Splits Percentage Bets 22% Handle 38% Why bettors are backing Mahomes Mahomes has the shortest odds to win Comeback Player of the Year by a pretty wide margin, with his +185 odds sitting pretty high above Jayden Daniels’ +450 and Kyler Murray’s +600. So it isn’t much of a surprise that Mahomes accounts for a market-high 22% of the bets – twice as many bets as Murray in second. There is a sharp lean towards Mahomes, too, since he is drawing 38% of the handle. Analysis This is Patrick Mahomes we’re talking about. Prior to 2025, he had placed top-seven in MVP voting in five the previous seven seasons. He is coming off the worst campaign of his career – he recorded just six wins, 22 touchdowns, 3,587 yards and an 89.6 passing rating – as well as a torn ACL in December. If Mahomes can guide Kansas City back to the playoffs and just come close to the 13 wins, 4,581 yards and 35 touchdowns he was averaging between 2018 and 2024, that should be enough for him to take home some hardware. When it comes to direct competition, I like Mahomes to reemerge rather than more slight, injury-prone hopefuls like Daniels and Murray. Aaron Donald unretiring is still a question mark, too, as is his potential impact should he rejoin the Rams after all. The narrative is also on Mahomes’ side, plus the fact that quarterbacks won the award seven straight years from 2018 to 2024. Drew Brees, Tom Brady, Peyton Manning, Andrew Luck and Joe Burrow have all won CPOTY in the past 20 years, and it only feels fitting for Mahomes to join that club.
